speaker: alse_pinder
text: The copper is on, sir. She has the galls in.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Galls, copperas, and gum. The same receipt as every Monday since you took the room. It comes up browner in November.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Browner than March. That is the one I want in the horn.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Twopence the horn, and you will not tell me the spring was kinder. Bring the brass one down.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Twopence. There it is. The horn is empty from the week.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I will fill it when the scum is off. Do not dip a pen in it while it is angry.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not dipping it this morning. I am Egeon at two, and idle after I have opened.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Idle is a player's word for standing in a passage. Eat before you go. The board is threepence, and I do not keep a dinner for a man who has already left for Shoreditch.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Threepence, and I will sit. The firing is the sixpence, and I am not starting a new column for it.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: The sixpence is the firing from Michaelmas to Lady Day, and it is paid. You will not recite it at my table as if you had invented it.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The loaf is cut. It is still a penny, and still short of the notch. I said so yesterday.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Once was enough for a baker. What do you want carried before Tuesday?

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Nothing today. Tuesday, when you have finished being clever upstairs, you will come down and be useful. Today you will open your play and hold your tongue in it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I open it. I do not stay in it. The end is other men's.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Then I will have your shoes by the door at one, and a clean band.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: At one. The book upstairs stays shut till after supper.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: After supper you may have the browner ink, and not before. I will not have you walk a wet page to the Theatre.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: After supper. The page that wants it is not this morning's page.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Gib is on the Chaucer. I did not move him. The slip still says lent, not given.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Leave the cat, and leave the book. That slip is none of your errand today.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not reading him. I am going to open a play, and then I am coming home.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Come home hungry and not proud. The horn will be full. The twopence is entered. That is the whole of the morning's trade.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I will sand the board when you have eaten. Do not thank the ink. It is oak-gall, and it smells of it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not thank it. I will use it when the house is quiet.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: The house is quiet when you are out of it. Sit, and eat, and go.
